transcript.text: Hi, our integrated fridge freezer (behind a kitchen door) - the fridge is around 10 degrees but the freezer seems ok. We had a power cut a week ago, not sure if related. Rented flat, can't really take it out.

That sounds like a cooling distribution issue where cold air isn't reaching the fridge compartment properly. Since it’s integrated and you can’t move it, the most common causes are blocked vents inside or a setting that got changed during or after the power cut. Please check if any food items are pressing against the back wall of the fridge or if the shelves are packed too tightly, blocking airflow. Also, double-check the temperature controls to ensure neither compartment is in an "eco" or holiday mode. Let me know if you find anything blocked or if the settings look correct.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

Thanks. There's just a dial inside, no eco or holiday mode that I can see, and it's on 3 of 5. Food isn't packed tight against the back as far as I know. No burning smell or tripping either, if that matters.

Since those checks didn't resolve the issue, we need to identify your specific appliance to find the correct parts or troubleshooting steps. Could you please provide the make and model number? This is usually found on a sticker inside the fridge, often on a side wall near the salad drawer. If you can't reach it right now because of the kitchen door, that's fine and we can wait.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I found the label inside the fridge - it's a Hotpoint HMCB 7030 AA. Does that help?

Yes, that model number helps significantly as we can now look at its specific design. Since you've checked the settings and food placement without success, the next likely cause is a blocked air vent or drain. On this Hotpoint model, cold air from the freezer enters the fridge through vents on the back wall, often near the bottom of the fridge section. Please check if there is any ice buildup around these vents or if they are obstructed by food items.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I can't see any vents on the back wall of the fridge, so I'm not sure where they'd be. There's some frost on the back of the freezer but not loads. Is that what you mean?

The vents are usually behind the plastic panel inside the fridge section, so it’s good you’ve checked there. The frost on the back of the freezer is normal, but if it builds up into a solid block, it can block airflow and warm up the fridge. Since you mentioned some frost, let's do a full manual defrost to clear any hidden ice blocking the vents or drain. Please switch the appliance off at the socket, move food to cool bags, and leave both doors open until all the ice has melted completely.
I can do that but I'd have to empty everything out first, so I haven't tried it yet. Is that definitely the next step? The freezer is at about -16C if that helps.

A manual defrost isn't most likely the final step yet, but it is the best way to check for hidden ice blocking the airflow from the freezer. Since you can see some frost in the freezer and the fridge is warm, a blockage there could be stopping cold air from reaching your food. Please switch the appliance off at the socket, move the food into cool bags with towels underneath, and leave both doors open until all the ice has melted completely.
